payload.text:
I reviewed `excerpt-helper` against `main` (2 commits) and didn't change anything. The tests pass, but I wouldn't merge yet: the main excerpt function has a bug that every card will hit.

**Must fix**

1. **Every preview gets a "…", even when nothing was cut.** In `src/excerpt.js`, `excerpt()` always adds the ellipsis. `excerpt('hi', 10)` returns `"hi…"`. The README says text at or under the limit comes back unchanged and the "…" only appears when something was removed, so short card bodies will look truncated when they aren't. It needs an early `if (trimmed.length <= limit) return trimmed;`.

2. **It cuts one word too early when a word ends exactly at the limit.** In `src/words.js`, `lastSpaceBefore` only searches `text.slice(0, limit)`, so it misses a space sitting right at position `limit`. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `"one…"` instead of `"one two…"`, which also breaks the README's "at or before the limit". Searching `slice(0, limit + 1)` would fix it. The existing test in `test/words.test.js` actually expects the wrong value (3) for this exact case, so that test needs updating too.

**Worth a look**

3. **Markdown cleanup removes characters that are part of the text.** In `src/plain.js`, `toPlain` deletes every `*`, `_`, `~` and backtick, wherever it appears. So `snake_case` becomes `snakecase` and `2*3` becomes `23`. It also leaves headings and list markers in place: `# Title\n- item` becomes `# Title - item`. Whether that matters depends on what your card bodies usually contain.

4. **Tests are thin.** There's one happy-path test per file. None cover short text, a word ending exactly at the limit, a single long word with no spaces (that currently gets cut mid-word, e.g. `abcde…`, which is probably fine), or empty input. Tests for these would have caught #1 and #2.

**Minor**

- `CHANGELOG.md` rewords an old 1.4.0 entry ("a title and a body" → "title and body"). It's harmless but unrelated to this change.
- The version bump to 1.5.0 and the README text look fine.
